tree.heading: Bureau
tree.text: The term “Bureau” means the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

tree.heading: Director
tree.text: The term “Director” means the Director of the Bureau.

tree.heading: First certified title status report
tree.text: The term “first certified title status report” means the title status report needed to verify title status on Indian land.

tree.heading: Indian land
tree.text: The term “Indian land” has the meaning given the term in section 162.003 of title 25, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on May 4, 2026).

tree.heading: Land mortgage
tree.text: The term “land mortgage” means a mortgage obtained by an individual Indian who owns a tract of trust land for the purpose of—

tree.heading: Leasehold mortgage
tree.text: The term “leasehold mortgage” means a mortgage, deed of trust, or other instrument that pledges the leasehold interest of a lessee as security for a debt or other obligation owed by the lessee to a lender or other mortgagee.

tree.heading: Mortgage package
tree.text: The term “mortgage package” means a proposed residential leasehold mortgage, business leasehold mortgage, land mortgage, or right-of-way document submitted to an applicable Bureau office under section 5902(a)(1) of this title.

tree.heading: Relevant Federal agency
tree.text: The term “relevant Federal agency” means any of the following Federal agencies that guarantee or make direct mortgage loans on Indian land:

children.text: The Department of Housing and Urban Development.

tree.heading: Right-of-way document
tree.text: The term “right-of-way document” has the meaning given the term in section 169.2 of title 25, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on May 4, 2026).

tree.heading: Subsequent certified title status report
tree.text: The term “subsequent certified title status report” means the title status report needed to identify any liens against a residential, business, or land lease on Indian land.

notes.text: Short TitlePub. L. 119–88, § 1, May 4, 2026, 140 Stat. 812, provided that: “This Act [enacting this chapter] may be cited as the ‘Tribal Trust Land Homeownership Act of 2025’.”
